items.name: Prediction-of-cement-compressive-strength-using-stacked-ensemble-modelling
items.description: The actual concrete compressive strength (MPa) for a given mixture under aspecific age (days) was determined from laboratory. Data is in raw form (not scaled).The data has 8 quantitative input variables, and 1 quantitative output variable, and 1030 instances (observations).Context:Concrete is the most important material in civil engineering. The concrete compressive strength is a highly nonlinear function of age and ingredients. These ingredients include cement, blast furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate. Summary of steps taken and performance achieved: Multiple models with different levels of complexity were attempted. The dependent and independent variables seem to have a nonlinear relationship as the performance of models improved with increasing complexity. MAPE was selected as the evaluation metric.Regularization, feature selection and hyper-parameter tuning was employed to improve the model performance. The models attempted are Linear Regression with no regularization Ridge and Lasso Gradient Boosting Random Forest XGboost Support Vector Machine Stacking - ensemble of the best estimators of the above tuned models with a meta regressor (i.e. Ridge) which gave the best result (MAPE of less than 10)

items.name: Bankruptcy-Prediction-Using-Financial-KPIs-ML-Pipeline-with-SMOTE-PCA-Stacked-Ensemble
items.description: Can financial ratios predict company bankruptcy before it happens? This end-to-end ML pipeline processes 95 financial KPIs from 6,800+ Taiwanese companies applying PCA, SMOTE+undersampling, and a stacked ensemble classifier to predict bankruptcy with high recall and strong ROC AUC.

items.name: Stacking-Ensemble-Groundwater-Prediction
items.description: This repository implements a hybrid stacking ensemble for accurate groundwater level prediction using tree-based machine learning models. It includes detailed data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, and overfitting analysis, all built with Python libraries like scikit-learn, XGBoost, and pandas.
